title: Branch-scoped development data
human_summary: Repobox gives every local Git branch persistent remote PostgreSQL data while application processes remain local. The first implementation uses PlanetScale and Docker Compose through a terminal-only Rust CLI that is equally operable by humans and agents.
machine_summary: Repobox uses PlanetScale OAuth device or service-token authentication, maps repository and Git identities to isolated Postgres branches, rewrites Compose in memory, persists resumable jobs, and exposes versioned JSON and JSONL contracts.
retrieval_hints: PlanetScale device login OAuth browser authentication

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Repobox provisions branch-scoped remote data and runs local services through one terminal contract.

sections.title: Decision required
sections.summary: Confirms the v0.1 provider, architecture, pull, and agent-contract boundaries.

sections.title: Problem and user need
sections.summary: Local databases are resource-heavy, shared across branches, and difficult for agents to acquire safely.

sections.title: Current behavior
sections.summary: Repositories use bespoke Compose, env-file, copy, and recovery conventions.

sections.title: Proposed behavior
sections.summary: Defines detection, environment identity, OAuth and service-token authentication, provider restore, credentials, Compose transformation, pull, and output behavior.

sections.title: Affected capabilities
sections.summary: Adds branch data, agent operation, local orchestration, and durable job recovery.

sections.title: Affected systems and components
sections.summary: Maps changes across the CLI, core, PlanetScale adapter, Compose adapter, and repository files.

sections.title: API and data model changes
sections.summary: Introduces strict YAML plus versioned success, mutation, stream, error, and job contracts.

sections.title: Architecture diagrams
sections.summary: Shows the local control plane and its internal provider/runtime boundaries.

sections.title: Alternatives considered
sections.summary: Rejects Go, local-only state, a daemon, on-disk rewrites, Terraform UX, and delete-first pull.

sections.title: Risks and mitigations
sections.summary: Covers provider cost, destructive refresh, partial work, secrets, public OAuth-client dependency, Compose semantics, terminal safety, and API drift.

sections.title: Rollout and migration plan
sections.summary: Stages offline verification, live provider smoke, artifact publication, compatibility, and rollback.

sections.title: Test plan
sections.summary: Defines unit, wire, black-box, CI, and release-gating live tests.

sections.title: Observability and operations
sections.summary: Uses local state, append-only jobs, structured output, request IDs, and diagnostic commands.

sections.title: Security and privacy review
sections.summary: Separates public device handoff values from access tokens, keeps secrets out of argv and repositories, revokes browser tokens, and makes unmasked data import explicit.

sections.title: Open questions
